still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has still approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US. Generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market, and exclusivity still runs to roughly 2031–32.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there. Maintenance doses went up; starting doses did not.
The suicidal-ideation warning is still off the Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels, and the finalised 503B compounding exclusion still stands. It held even through the 2029 pen shortage.

The September 2027 Labor/HHS/Treasury guidance still lets employer wellness programmes tie up to a 30% premium differential to verified adherence or BMI. Only Illinois and, since 2029, California ban this under state law.

population.note: FICTIONAL estimates. Arithmetic: 25.5% ever-used − 17.5% current = 8.0% of adults (~21M) who have used the drugs and are off now. 46% of ever-users have cycled, which is 11.7 points: ~9.4 points are current users on at least their second course (54% of current users), and ~2.3 points have cycled and are off again. That leaves ~5.7 points who stopped once and never restarted. This fits roughly one-third persistence at one year and 36–47% restarting within a year, compounded. New ever-users over the two years: 3.5 points (~9.3M people). 17.5% of ~267M adults is ~46.7M current users. Payer mix: commercial ~29% (~13.5M, down from ~14M as employers retreat; mostly diabetes and cardiac codes), Medicare ~21% (~9.8M, up ~1.8M, of which ~1.4M came through the tirzepatide dementia-risk Part D route), Medicaid ~7% (~3.3M; 7 states still cover weight management), legitimate cash ~38% (~17.7M), imported or counterfeit ~5% (~2.3M, down from ~3M after the India export controls). 13.5 + 9.8 + 3.3 + 17.7 + 2.3 = 46.6M. Age-weighted check (adult shares ~20/33/24/23%): 2.0 + 5.6 + 6.5 + 3.45 ≈ 17.5. Income-weighted check: (24 + 18 + 10.5)/3 = 17.5. The bottom third fell from 11% to 10.5% after losing gray-market product, Medicaid opt-ins and employer tracks; the middle third rose on $149–349 cash orals. Adult obesity is ~34.0%. About 25% of adults still have obesity and have never used a drug, concentrated in the bottom income third and the South. Under-18 use is ~1.0%, almost all ages 12–17, still skewed toward upper-income households.

access.public_coverage: Medicare covers incretins under diabetes, cardiovascular, CKD, sleep-apnoea and, since Aug 2028, tirzepatide's dementia-risk label, behind prior authorisation. There is no Medicare weight-loss benefit. Dementia route: ~1.4M beneficiaries × ~$450 net/month after rebates × 12 ≈ $7.6B annualised Part D spend by end-2030. That is why CMS added a DXA-before-renewal step to the PA criteria in 2030. Medicaid: of the 14 states that opted in at $245 in 2027, 7 still cover weight management, and 2 of those require adherence and BMI progress. DoD covers supervised orals for service members under the Feb 2030 Metabolic Readiness instruction: ~85,000 enrolled × ~$160/month DLA contract price × 12 ≈ $163M/yr.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide is still $6–40/month domestically, with 70+ brands. Generics are in ~175 countries, and India and China supply most of the world's volume. Since the Sep 2029 US–India interim trade agreement, India requires export no-objection certificates and bars courier shipment of unapproved incretins to US personal addresses. That has not touched supply to the rest of the world.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Price shock up. A sterility failure at Novo's Clayton, NC fill-finish plant (Apr 2029) caused a Wegovy/Ozempic pen shortage from May to Dec 2029. TrumpRx injectable semaglutide cash prices reset from $299–449 to $399–599. The Wegovy pill maintenance dose rose from $299 to $349 (the $149 starting dose was untouched). Zepbound vial cash prices rose to $449–649 as Lilly rationed injectable capacity toward retatrutide and the new combination. FDA listed only specific pen strengths as in shortage and said compounding remained barred under the 503B exclusion, citing oral semaglutide as an alternative; the Outsourcing Facilities Association's suit was dismissed. Gray-market delivered prices roughly doubled, from ~$40–80 to ~$90–160 a month, after India's export controls; counterfeit pens briefly surged during the shortage. Employer weight-management coverage is down to 35% (Business Group on Health 2030); about a third of that runs through monitored tracks. Adherence-verified enrollees fell from ~3M to ~2.4M, inside ~13.5M commercial users. Orals are now ~55% of all users and ~65% of new starts. Combination tirzepatide + bimagrumab lists at $2,280, with LillyDirect cash at $1,099; it is not on TrumpRx and most plans exclude it.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved Mar 2029 with dysesthesia warning)
Tirzepatide + bimagrumab (activin type II receptor antibody), weekly + monthly subcutaneous co-pack (approved May 2030 for chronic weight management in adults 50+)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established cardiovascular disease (tirzepatide, Aug 2028; confirmatory trial enrolling, no new indication since)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol reduction via telehealth and EAPs; oral semaglutide AUD phase 3 read out positive in 2030, sNDA filed, not approved
dementia-prevention use by 55–70-year-olds without cardiovascular disease, cash-paid on orals
microdosing and 'flex dosing' (planned skip days) marketed by telehealth to manage flatness
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
bimagrumab-combo use by under-50s and normal-BMI 'recomposition' seekers, cash-paid
drugs.pipeline_note: The muscle_preserving_combo driver arrived the only way the rules allow, as a new combination for an existing indication. Lilly filed tirzepatide + bimagrumab in Mar 2029 and got approval in May 2030. The label indication is chronic weight management in adults 50+ with obesity. The clinical-studies section shows lean mass making up ~10% of weight lost versus ~30% on tirzepatide alone, with similar total loss (~21%). There are no fracture, bone-density-preservation or physical-function outcomes, and FDA declined a 'preservation of muscle' indication. DTC ads ('Lose the fat. Keep you.') drew an OPDP untitled letter in Aug 2030. About 180k users by end-2030, supply-limited and mostly cash or executive plans. Retatrutide was approved Mar 2029 for weight management only (~26% at 68–80 weeks), with a dysesthesia warning; its higher absolute lean-mass loss feeds the bone debate. Survodutide got a CRL in Jul 2029 over hepatic safety data; BI resubmitted in Jun 2030. Amycretin was filed Nov 2029; the decision was extended to Feb 2031. Amgen filed MariTide in Apr 2030, so it is not on the market. No oral matches tirzepatide. Novo and Lilly remain the only branded US sellers. Global incretin market ~$135B (2029).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Retatrutide's GI rates are higher at top doses, and the bimagrumab combo adds diarrhoea.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
Absolute risk low; no causal confirmation. The MDL settled in 2029 without admission.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Now recognised as a population problem. A 2029 three-year Medicare cohort update put the hip-fracture HR at ~1.4 in women 65+ with >3 years' continuous use (~1.3 in all users 65+). Rough excess: ~5M long-term users 65+ × ~0.5% baseline annual hip-fracture rate × ~0.3 excess ≈ 7,500 extra hip fractures a year, against ~300k US hip fractures overall. Sarcopenia codes in users 70+ have roughly tripled since 2025. 'Skinny-frail' is common usage. Risk concentrates in older women, people on low protein, retatrutide users and repeated cyclers who regain as fat (sarcopenic obesity).
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The July 2028 class warning was retained. In Nov 2029 the American Geriatrics Society Beers Criteria added incretins as 'use with caution' in adults 75+ with osteoporosis or falls. In 2030 CMS required DXA before renewal on the dementia-route PA. Senate Aging Committee hearing (Jan 2030). FDA has not issued a boxed warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA adverse-reactions listing.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: A 2029 randomised dose-taper trial (n≈3,100) confirmed dose-dependence. Anhedonia scores improved in ~60% of affected users within 8 weeks of stepping down a dose. Clinically meaningful prevalence stays ~6–8% of users, higher on retatrutide. A much larger share reports milder flatness.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA added anhedonia/apathy to adverse reactions (section 6) in Apr 2030, with no warning. The postmarketing observational study continues.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. The 2029 shortage and the gray-market squeeze forced ~1M involuntary stops, and their regain shows in 2030 data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; supports the chronic-therapy framing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Case series continue (B12, iron, vitamin D, protein insufficiency), especially in low-dose and gray-market users.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; adolescents on decades-long therapy; repeated cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About eight years of follow-up exists. Interim (24-month) adolescent DXA data from the 2028 postmarketing requirement show BMD accrual below age norms in a subset; uninterpretable so far without matched weight-loss controls.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric PMR continues; AAP 2030 statement urges DXA at baseline and 12 months for adolescents.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Counterfeit pen reports spiked during the 2029 shortage (~2,100 reports in 8 months). Mg/unit dosing errors are still the commonest poison-centre call. Volume fell after India's export controls, but per-user risk did not.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA import alert, CBP seizures, India export NOC regime, state marketplace suits.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone stress injury in young, highly active users (military trainees, police academies)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: An Army Public Health Center surveillance memo (2030) noted higher tibial and metatarsal stress-fracture rates among Metabolic Readiness enrollees in their first 16 weeks. Confounded by enrollees' starting fitness.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: DoD bars initiation during basic training, and requires DXA and a strength block at enrollment.

safety_ledger.effect: Tirzepatide + bimagrumab specific effects (muscle spasms, diarrhoea, acne, unknown bone and long-term muscle-quality effects)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Spasms in ~30% of trial users early on. Lean mass is preserved on DXA, but no strength, function or fracture outcomes exist. Effect on hip BMD unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; postmarketing fracture and function study required.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Skin dysesthesia in a minority at higher doses, mostly transient; it drives discontinuation.

food_and_beverage.state: About 32% of households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~6–8% from 2025, and sugary drinks ~7%. Pricing and protein lines keep dollar sales near flat. Protein is now a class-coded category: whey and 'lean-mass' ranges sit at premium price points in upscale grocers, while discount chains carry cheap high-protein private label. The 2029 shortage briefly lifted snack volumes in Ohio and Texas scanner data as involuntary stoppers regained appetite.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~10% from 2025 and beer ~6%. DOT's 2029 interpretation that stable off-label incretin use does not disqualify CDL holders cemented trucking-firm EAP programmes. Brown-Forman closed another US bottling line. Non-alcoholic lines and small premium pours are the growth segment. Weekend 'holiday-day' drinking makes Saturday sales spikier.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat and checks are smaller. Protein-forward menus are standard, and high-end steakhouses market 'recomposition plates'. Buffets keep closing. Saturday-night covers are up relative to weeknights, which operators attribute to drug-holiday dining.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. The growth line is structured, muscle-showing athleisure in Lululemon and Vuori price tiers. Value chains sell multi-size stretch basics to cyclers. Shoulders are back in tailoring as a status cut.

fitness.state: Strength gyms, DXA chains and 'lean-mass clinics' grow, concentrated in affluent metros (Scottsdale, Austin, North Shore Chicago) where combo prescribing is bundled with trainers. Planet Fitness's rack conversion continues. Medicare Advantage plans add strength-class benefits after the Beers update.

insurance.state: Employer weight-management coverage is down to 35%. Pharmacy trend was ~+10% in 2029 on shortage-era price resets. Coverage concentrates on diabetes, cardiac and dementia codes. Monitored tracks shrank after the California ban and exits by logistics and call-centre employers. Nearly all commercial plans exclude the bimagrumab combo. Medicare actuaries now model dementia-route spend (~$7.6B annualised) against fracture costs.

pharma.state: Lilly gained share through retatrutide, the combo and Novo's shortage. Novo's US injectable revenue fell in 2029 and its oral business held. US net prices rose; ex-US prices kept falling under generics. Indian makers lost US mail volume to export controls but gained in Africa and Southeast Asia.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: A lean body with visible shoulders reads as top-tier: insured or cash-rich, on tirzepatide or the combo, with DXA scans and a trainer. A thin, soft body in someone over 60 reads as 'on it without the extras', and increasingly as frail. A regained body reads as a lapsed plan or a shortage casualty. Untreated obesity reads, more than ever, as a low income.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Class uniforms have set. Muscle is the new marker, because thinness is now cheap at $149 a month and muscle preservation costs $1,099 or a trainer. In Columbus, Ohio, where two large logistics employers ended metabolic tracks in 2029, warehouse workers are visibly regaining while their managers' managers post DXA results. In The Villages, Florida, hip fractures in thin older women have become a local talking point, and church groups run strength classes. Upper-income teenagers are both the most medicated and the most gym-trained youth cohort.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Meals stay small. The new ritual is the planned skip day: Saturday dinners, holidays and anniversaries become the days people go off their dose to eat, so feasting is now scheduled. The 'Bread Alone' church fasting network claims ~500 congregations. Protein counting has replaced calorie counting in middle-class kitchens.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: App profiles now list 'on / off / flexing'. Body composition, not weight, is a dating signal in upscale metros. Desire mismatch is still a common reason couples seek therapy, and couples increasingly align skip days.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is still split between 'noise' and 'aliveness', but the argument has shifted toward class. Critics on left and right say the affluent buy back both muscle and pleasure (combo plus scheduled holidays), while everyone else gets flat and fragile. The Unmuted collective's 'off nights' have spread to Detroit and Oakland.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Clinically meaningful anhedonia in ~6–8% of users, confirmed as dose-dependent and partly reversible in a 2029 taper trial; it is now in the label's adverse reactions section. Survey data (2030) suggest ~35% of current users deliberately skip or step down doses at least monthly to feel 'more like themselves', and daily orals make single-day holidays easy.
interior_life.framing: Mostly a side effect, managed by dosing. 'Flat' and 'flexing' are everyday words. Telehealth firms sell 'flex dosing' plans with programmed skip days. The 'steadiness' HR framing survives in the remaining monitored tracks and in DoD readiness language, but is mocked in mainstream culture.
interior_life.effect_on_work: About 2.4M employees remain in adherence-verified tracks. Fill data cannot detect skip days, so verified adherence overstates actual use, and vendors are pushing app-linked pill logs. The EEOC settled one ADA charge in 2029 with a reasonable-alternative commitment; the other is in litigation. Managers talk openly about 'Monday flatness' after weekend holidays. Police departments in Phoenix and Fort Worth offer supervised orals; their unions bargained a no-discipline clause for dose reductions.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Flat' fiction has turned into a comic genre of satire about skip-day hedonism. Sportsbooks see a Saturday wagering spike among identifiable users. The Unmuted 'off nights' now draw corporate sponsors. Music critics write about a 'loud weekend, quiet weekday' release cycle.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples schedule sex and celebrations around skip days, and therapists report 'calendar intimacy' as both a fix and a complaint. Partners on different tiers (one on the combo, one on gray-market vials) describe class friction in the bedroom.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: California's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums passed in 2029. A federal bill to codify such bans has bipartisan sponsors and no floor vote. The Senate Aging hearing on 'skinny-frail' gave MAHA-aligned legislators and geriatricians common ground. Some veterans' groups support the DoD readiness programme and others, joined by some progressives, oppose it. There is still no measurable effect on turnout.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-speed on new molecules (retatrutide, the combo) but holding the line on indications: no new indication, and the combo's muscle claim was refused. Rhetorically hard on imports, now with Indian export controls behind it. FDA refused to reopen compounding during the 2029 pen shortage.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No civilian mandate and no Medicare weight benefit. Public money flows through disease codes: Medicare dementia route (~$7.6B annualised), DoD Metabolic Readiness (~$163M/yr). TrumpRx continues at reset prices. Federal tri-agency premium-differential guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: PBM fill data plus app-linked logs in ~2.4M employer-track enrollees, four state employee plans (Indiana dropped its track in 2030) and two Medicaid programmes. DoD enrollees take observed doses in initial-entry settings and logged doses afterwards, and body-composition and DXA data sit in readiness records.
state.workforce_or_military: The Feb 2030 DoD Instruction 'Metabolic Readiness' authorises supervised oral incretins for service members outside body-composition standards (~85,000 enrolled). It requires DXA, a 12-week strength block and protein counselling, and bars starting during basic training after the stress-fracture memo. The FAA allows pilots on a stable dose after a 30-day observation period. DOT treats stable off-label use by CDL holders as non-disqualifying. Several big-city police departments and hospital systems run supervised shift-worker programmes. During the 2029 shortage, DLA's priority allocation of Foundayo for the Army recruit pilot drew congressional criticism.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The Sep 2029 US–India interim trade agreement traded tariff relief on Indian generics for export controls on unapproved incretin mail to the US. China-sourced counterfeits partly filled the gap. Novo's Clayton failure exposed concentrated US fill-finish capacity, and manufacturers announced onshoring of further capacity in exchange for tariff treatment.

events.event: FDA halts injectable production at Novo Nordisk's Clayton, NC fill-finish plant after sterility failures; Wegovy and Ozempic pens go on the shortage list until December, TrumpRx injectable cash prices reset to $399–599 and Wegovy pill maintenance rises to $349; FDA refuses to reopen compounding

Business Group on Health survey finds employer weight-management coverage down to 36%, falling to 35% in 2030; two Columbus, Ohio logistics employers and Indiana's state plan end monitored metabolic tracks, citing post-shortage costs

US–India interim trade agreement requires Indian export certificates and bans courier shipment of unapproved semaglutide to US addresses; gray-market prices roughly double and imported-product users fall from ~3M to ~2.3M

Three-year Medicare cohort puts hip-fracture risk ~40% higher in women over 65 on long-term incretins; American Geriatrics Society adds the class to Beers Criteria for adults 75+ with osteoporosis or falls; Senate Aging hearing on 'skinny-frail' follows in January

Pentagon issues 'Metabolic Readiness' instruction authorising supervised oral GLP-1s for service members outside body-composition standards, with mandatory DXA and strength training; ~85,000 enrolled by year end, initiation barred in basic training after stress-fracture memo

FDA approves Lilly's tirzepatide-plus-bimagrumab co-pack for weight management in adults 50+, citing preserved lean mass on DXA but no fracture or function data; $1,099 cash, excluded by most plans; FDA later warns Lilly over 'Keep you' ads

open_tensions: The combo is sold as the fix for skinny-frail, but it has DXA lean-mass data without fracture or function outcomes, costs $1,099 cash, and is out of reach for the older, lower-income users the bone wave hits hardest. Medicare will be asked to cover it.

Medicare's dementia route keeps adding beneficiaries 65+ (~$7.6B annualised) while the Beers Criteria and the hip-fracture cohort say the oldest users are most harmed. CMS's DXA-before-renewal rule is the only brake.

The military and police treat the drug as readiness infrastructure. That puts it into young, highly loaded skeletons, with a stress-fracture signal and a precedent of priority allocation during shortages.

Premiums are still tied to fill-verified adherence while ~35% of users deliberately skip doses to manage flatness. Pressure is building for pill-level surveillance, and for a federal ban, as the bottom income third falls further off the drug.

prose.headline: Thin Is Cheap Now. Muscle Costs $1,099 a Month.
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2030, a little over one American adult in six takes an incretin drug, and one in four has tried one. Most of them take a pill. The $149 starting dose of oral Wegovy is still on the government's cash site, and it is still how most people begin. Almost everything after the first month costs more than it did two years ago. In April 2029 the FDA shut down injectable production at Novo Nordisk's North Carolina fill-finish plant after sterility failures, and pens were scarce until December. Novo raised cash prices when the plant came back and did not lower them again. Lilly raised its own. Oral maintenance doses went from $299 to $349. The FDA refused to let compounders fill the gap, saying the pill was an alternative. The pill was an alternative for people who could pay for it.

People who couldn't pay had been buying Indian generic vials by mail. Those vials got harder to find in September, when a trade deal with India brought export controls on shipments to American homes. Mail-order prices doubled. About seven hundred thousand people dropped out of the gray market. Some of them moved to cash pills, and many simply stopped. Employers kept leaving too. Only about a third now cover the drugs for weight loss. The rest of commercial coverage runs on diabetes and heart codes. In Columbus, Ohio, two big logistics companies ended their monitored 'metabolic tracks', and the regain is visible on warehouse floors.

The skeleton is the new problem. A three-year Medicare study found that older women on the drugs long-term broke hips about forty percent more often. The geriatrics society's list of drugs to use cautiously in the very old now includes them. That works out to several thousand extra hip fractures a year, against a national total of three hundred thousand. It is small in the national count and large in the Villages, where thin women in their seventies swap fracture stories at strength classes their churches organise. Meanwhile Medicare's other door keeps opening. About 1.4 million beneficiaries now take tirzepatide under its dementia-risk label, and CMS has started requiring a bone scan before each renewal.

In May, Lilly brought the answer it had been promising. The FDA approved tirzepatide co-packaged with bimagrumab, an antibody that kept lean mass on body scans in trials. Patients lost about as much weight with far less muscle. The agency approved it for weight loss, not for muscle, and later reprimanded Lilly over ads that said 'Keep you.' Nobody has fracture or strength data yet. It costs $1,099 a month in cash, and nearly every insurer excludes it. It has become the drug of executives and lean-mass clinics in Scottsdale and Austin. So the class ladder now has a top rung. A lean, shouldered body says money and a trainer. A thin, soft one past sixty says the cheap tier. A regained one says the plan lapsed or the pens ran out. Untreated obesity now marks a low income more clearly than ever.

The flatness is no longer a whispered side effect. A 2029 taper trial confirmed that it scales with dose and lifts when people step down, and it is now on the label. Roughly a third of users skip doses on purpose, usually on Saturdays, so feasting has become a calendar event. Telehealth sells 'flex dosing'. The remaining employer tracks verify fills, which say nothing about the pills skipped on weekends. California banned premiums tied to adherence. The Pentagon went the other way. Its Metabolic Readiness programme puts 85,000 service members on supervised pills, with bone scans and squat requirements, after an Army memo about stress fractures in new enrollees. Police departments and hospitals copy it. From a distance the country looks leaner, steadier and more disciplined. Close up it is sorted by who can afford the extras.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Okafor's pill bottle has a Saturday compartment, and she leaves it full.

She is fifty-eight, a dispatcher at a freight yard on Columbus's south side. The yard ended its metabolic track last fall. The $349 now comes off her own card through TrumpRx on the fourth of every month, the same day as the car payment. She has priced the new Lilly combo and closed the tab.

At seven she drives her mother to the Riverside imaging centre. Her mother is eighty-one, on tirzepatide through Medicare because of her heart and the dementia thing, and she needs a bone scan before the pharmacy will refill. Her mother sits on the paper sheet and asks whether they'll take the brain medicine away if the bones are bad. The technician says that's for the doctor.

In the waiting room a television plays the ad with the man doing pull-ups. Lose the fat. Keep you. Her mother says he looks like a fireman. Denise says he looks like a man with a trainer.

At noon Denise eats half a turkey wrap and logs eighty grams of protein toward a target she misses most days.

The dispatch board is quiet in a way she can't describe. Her supervisor calls it Monday flat, and it is Saturday.

At six her nephew's graduation party opens with smoked brisket and tres leches. She hasn't taken today's pill, and by the second plate she can taste the cumin. Her sister, who stopped when the mail vials dried up, is heavier and laughing louder than anyone. Denise takes a third piece of cake and watches her.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Rough excess: ~5M long-term users 65+ × ~0.5% baseline annual hip-fracture rate × ~0.3 excess ≈ 7,500 extra hip fractures a year, against ~300k US hip fractures overall.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: about 9M adults 65+ are on the drug, and persistence is roughly one-third at one year with 46% cycling. Having ~5M of them on more than 3 years of continuous use contradicts the world's own cycling arithmetic, so the excess-fracture figure rests on an inflated base.

least_plausible_claims.quote: four state employee plans (Indiana dropped its track in 2030)
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the 2029-08 event says Indiana's state plan ended its monitored track in 2029, not 2030. The world contradicts itself on the date.

least_plausible_claims.quote: FDA halts injectable production at Novo Nordisk's Clayton, NC fill-finish plant after sterility failures
least_plausible_claims.why: Driver fidelity and mechanism: a plant failure causing an eight-month national shortage is a convenient exogenous supply shock, and it sits uneasily with the stipulated market_shock of none. It carries nearly the whole price_path and employer-cost story.

rationale.badness: The world sorts people by class at every level. Muscle preservation costs $1,099 a month while thinness is cheap. Thousands of excess hip fractures a year, a 'skinny-frail' older population, about 1M involuntary stops and regain, a bottom-third decline, and ~35% of users managing flatness by skipping doses make it a recognisably harder society. The harms are measured and discussed in the Beers Criteria, the Senate hearing and the label changes, so the epistemic score stays low and the overall stays near 6. The main losers are low-income and older users, and the military stress-fracture signal adds a small autonomy cost.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: All ten drivers are visibly realised. The shortage and price reset, the 44→35% employer retreat, the bone wave, the combo (filed Mar 2029, approved May 2030) and the military instruction are all traceable. The Clayton shortage (claim 3) sits awkwardly against market_shock of none, which costs a point or two. mechanism: Most chains are shown, such as shortage to price reset to retreat, and India controls to gray-market prices and user decline. Weaknesses are the convenient shortage trigger (claim 3), the Indiana date contradiction (claim 2), and the prose saying prices rose when the plant 'came back' while the event dates the reset to the shortage. magnitude: Current use of 17.5% and ever-use of 25.5% are inside the envelope, and the income and age checks, payer mix (46.6M), dementia spend (~$7.6B) and DoD spend (~$163M) all multiply out. The main gap is the ~5M long-term 65+ users in the fracture arithmetic (claim 1), which conflicts with the cycling and persistence figures. Pipeline timings (retatrutide, survodutide, amycretin, the combo) are allowed by the rules.
rationale.generativity: The Denise Okafor scene gives concrete texture: the Saturday compartment, the $349 card charge on the fourth of the month, the mother's bone-scan appointment, the 'Keep you' ad, and the party where she can taste the cumin. Many other characters and places are implied, including the Columbus warehouse floors, The Villages strength classes, Scottsdale combo clinics, and the police and military programmes. The prose half is partly explanatory, and 'Monday flat' on a Saturday is slightly muddled, but the world is rich in filmable material.
